label: copy-phase input t (fed-back output t) from recall step 3 on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input is the letter t (the model feeding back its own previous output t, i.e. original token recall_idx-1 is t) and recall_idx >= 3. It is essentially silent on t during the original phase or at the delimiter, on early copy steps (recall_idx <= 2), and on any other input token. Magnitude is smallest at recall_idx 3 (mass per activation about half of what later steps show) and larger for later positions. When two t tokens come in a row, the second one is weaker (about 0.6-0.7 of the first). The preceding token, the next output, and the first token have little effect.

issues: I reproduced the test scores exactly: P 0.976, R 0.993, F1 0.984, mass recall 0.999.

The claims about phase and token hold. On dev there are 0 activations in the original phase and 0 at the delimiter, and in_tok == t carries 100% of the activation mass (the next-highest token has 2 activations).

'Silent at recall_idx <= 2' is slightly overstated: there are 408 dev activations at recall_idx 2. They carry only 0.1% of the mass and are weak, with the largest shown about 0.12 of max (examples are L=3/4 with t at position 1), so this is small noise.

The false positives cluster at recall_idx 3: on test, 16157 predicted steps there have precision 0.914, while recall_idx >= 4 has precision 0.9996. So roughly 1.4k misfires sit at the onset step. They are spread across all L values (precision 0.87-0.96 for each L) and are not explained by prev_tok == t. This fits the weak-onset claim already in the explanation, so I don't count it as a separate counterexample class.
'Mass per activation at recall_idx 3 is about half' checks out: mass/recall is about 0.48 at recall_idx 3 versus about 1.19 at recall_idx >= 4, a ratio of roughly 0.4.
The repeated-t claim is weakly supported: when prev_tok == t, mass per activation is about 0.83 of the average. That is in the claimed direction, but I did not confirm the exact 0.6-0.7 ratio.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
